messages.subject: Fun with a babynames function...
parts:
Hey y'all,

My best friend is having a baby (boy), and I want to annoy her with lots of name suggestions (especially weird, 19th-century name suggestions ;).  I thought it would be a fun R/dplyr challenge to come up with a function or a bit of code that samples the 'babynames' package for 5 random boys' names from each decade (1880-2020), and send one group of names to her every day (bonus points if I can get R to Tweet them to her, but one step at a time here).

I can do it decade by one decade, manually:

library(babynames)
library(dplyr)
babynamess <- babynames

babynamess %>%
  filter(sex=='M') %>%
  filter(year<=1889) %>%
  sample_n(.,5)

...but I'd like to be able to write a function that pulls 5 names from each decade into a tbl_df.  My first problem is that I can't figure out how to get dplyr to add a 'decades' column, conditional on the year. Does anyone know how to do this?  I'm guessing it's some permutation of (summarize), but I don't know what.

Thanks, hopefully this provides a good little diversion for folks that need one, and I'll be at the drug meeting tomorrow!

Best,
Myfanwy

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Fun with a babynames function...
parts:
In dplyr, mutate is used to create new columns or update existing ones, then you’ll want group_by to sample from each decade:

library(babynames)
library(dplyr)
babynamess <- babynames

babynamess %>%
  filter(sex=='M') %>%
  mutate(decade = plyr::round_any(year, accuracy = 10, f = floor)) %>%
  group_by(decade) %>%
  sample_n(.,5)

I’m using the round_any function from the plyr package here because it’s a convenient way to round down to the nearest 10. Many plyr functions interfere with dplyr, though, so I don’t load the whole package but just get the one function with plyr::round_any.

Mazal Tov to your friend!

Noam
